rows.derivation: Pins the documented mode (CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-29: System.Decimal, exact within 28-29 digits, round-half-even beyond, no truncating division, final GR3 truncation; one evaluator for CONSTANT AS and >>DEFINE/>>IF). D1 2/3*3 -> 2 (truncating division would be 1); D2 100/7*7 -> 100 (99); D3 1/3*3 -> 0; T1 5E-28/2*1E28 -> 2 (tie-to-even; half-up 3); T2 15E-28/2*1E28 -> 8 (truncation 7); >>DEFINE D1V AS 2/3*3 then >>IF D1V = 2 selected. Negative: 28 nines * 10 exceeds the documented intermediate range -> COBOLNET1547, never wrapped.

rows.derivation: COBOL.NET defines no IMP directive, so no implementor syntax rule admits >>IMP, and SR6 admits a compiler-instruction only 'as specified in the syntax of each directive': '>>IMP SOMETHING' (column 8, fixed form) is not a directive and must be rejected at 2002/2014/2023. Control: the same file with '>>LISTING ON' in that position compiles and runs.
citations: cite.py --check 7.3.3 "The compiler-directive word 'IMP' is reserved for use by the implementor. If the implementor defines the IMP directive, the syntax rules for that directive shall be implementor-defined." -> OK §7.3.3 9)
cite.py --check 7.3.3 "Compiler-instruction is composed of compiler-directive words, system-names, and user-defined words as specified in the syntax of each directive" -> OK §7.3.3 6)
rows.notes: The .err is COBOL0001 (generic 'unexpected >' syntax error, the same code used by 10 existing negatives), NOT a COBOLNETnnnn code specific to this rule: the compiler has no dedicated 'unknown directive word' diagnostic. The director should decide whether a generic-syntax witness is acceptable; if not, move this row to not-closable. >>DEFINE IMP AS 1 being accepted is the SR-7.3.3-7 / 7.3.11.3 SR1 defect the adjudicator already charged elsewhere, not re-filed here.

rows.derivation: The interface prototype GETX returns OBJECT REFERENCE X ONLY. With an implementation that also returns X ONLY (the ONLY phrase and the same name), it conforms: it compiles, runs and prints SPEAK-L1C05RX. With an implementation returning X without ONLY, it does not conform (COBOLNET0841). With an implementation returning Y ONLY, where Y INHERITS X, it does not conform either: the name is not the same, and rule c) 2., which admits a subclass, applies only without ONLY (COBOLNET0841).
citations: cite.py --check 9.3.8.2.3 "If the returning item in interface-2 is described with the ONLY phrase, the returning item in interface-1 shall be described with the ONLY phrase and the same object-class-name" -> OK §9.3.8.2.3 5) 2. c)
cite.py --check 11.8.3 "Each method prototype in each implemented interface shall be such that the object interface of this class conforms to all implemented interfaces" -> OK §11.8.3 2)
rows.notes: Cosmetic only: the 0841 message for both negatives cites '(ISO §9.3.8.2.3 rules 5a/5c2)' and §14.9.39.3 SR12 a)1. The rule actually applied is 5 c) 1. The verdict is right; only the rule the message names is wrong (OoConformance.cs ObjectRefAssignmentMismatch).

rows.derivation: The interface and the implementing class declare ADDV with the same BY REFERENCE PIC 9(4) formal. The only difference is RETURNING: the prototype has it and the implementation lacks it, or the other way round. Either way presence differs, so the class does not conform (§11.8.3 SR2) and each is rejected with COBOLNET0841 at 2002, 2014 and 2023. Control: RETURNING on both sides compiles. The admitting case is already covered by conformance:2002/oo_interface_conformance.

rows.derivation: The prototype and the implementation each declare an equivalent TYPEDEF TT STRONG in their linkage section (§8.5.3.1). With the formal and returning item both of type TT, it conforms and runs: GOT=ABCD, RET=WXYZ. It does not conform (COBOLNET0841) when the formal is type TU, a strong type with the identical layout but another type-name. That case is distinctive to rule 7, since a non-strong group would pass rule 3. It also does not conform when the formal is a plain group of the same width, or when the RETURNING item is type TU.

rows.derivation: Admitting half: >>IF 7 / 2 = 3 is TRUE (3.5 truncates to 3, GR3). >>IF 1.5 + 0 = 1 is TRUE. >>IF 1 + 2 * 3 = 7 is TRUE (§8.8.1 precedence). >>IF -7 / 2 < -3 is FALSE (the integer part toward zero is -3; INTEGER would give -4). Rejecting halves, COBOLNET1619 at 2002, 2014 and 2023: SR1a '2 ** 2 = 4', SR1c '1 / 0 = 1', SR1b '"1" + 1 = 2'. Control: each negative with '1 + 1 = 2' compiles and selects.

cite.py --check 7.3.6.2 "The exponentiation operator shall not be specified" -> OK §7.3.6.2 1) a)
cite.py --check 7.3.6.2 "All operands shall be fixed-point numeric literals or arithmetic expressions in which all operands are fixed-point numeric literals" -> OK §7.3.6.2 1) b)

cite.py --check 7.3.6.3 "The final result of the arithmetic expression shall be truncated to the integer part of the value" -> OK §7.3.6.3 3)
rows.notes: The first drafts put >> at column 7, the fixed-form indicator area. That is illegal under §7.3.3 SR3 (cite OK §7.3.3 3): 'in the program-text area'. Once the header was wrapped to 72 columns, the file auto-detected as fixed and gave COBOL0001, so the drafts were moved to column 8 (a slip in my program, not a compiler defect). Hygiene note for the corpus: existing 2002/directive_expressions.cob also puts its directives at column 7. It passes only because its 115-character comment line makes the documented format auto-detection (ReferenceFormatProcessor.IsFixedForm) choose free form.

rows.derivation: Admitting half (§8.8.2 evaluation): B"1" B-XOR B"1" = B"0" is TRUE. B"1" = B"1" B-AND B"0" is FALSE. B"1100" B-OR B"0011" = B"1111" is TRUE. B-NOT B"0" B-AND B"0" = B"0" is TRUE because B-NOT binds first. B"1" B-OR B"1" B-XOR B"1" = B"1" is TRUE because XOR binds before OR; left to right would give FALSE. Rejecting half, COBOLNET1619 at 2002, 2014 and 2023: an alphanumeric "1" or a numeric 1 as a B-AND operand. Control: '1 + 1 = 2' compiles.
